values.value: You operated, maintained, or managed aircraft in demanding conditions where errors have serious consequences. Your experience covers flight operations, maintenance procedures, and the discipline that keeps both people and machines safe. You understand preflight planning, crew coordination, and the regulatory environment around aviation — skills that civilian aviation employers look for and cannot easily train from scratch.

[{"title": "Commercial Airline Pilot", "description": "You fly passengers or cargo on scheduled routes, manage the aircraft systems, and make safety decisions throughout the flight. Military pilots with 750+ flight hours qualify for a Restricted ATP under 14 CFR § 61.160, which authorizes you to serve as SIC at an airline. Full ATP at 1,500 hours is required for PIC. Rotary-wing hours alone do not satisfy the 250-hour fixed-wing PIC requirement, so helicopter-only backgrounds will need additional fixed-wing time before qualifying. Major carriers actively recruit transitioning military pilots."}, {"title": "Aircraft Mechanic (A&P)", "description": "You inspect, repair, and maintain aircraft airframes and powerplants, sign off on maintenance records, and ensure the aircraft is airworthy. Military aviation maintenance experience counts toward FAA A&P certification under 14 CFR § 65.77. The JSAMTCC (Joint Service Aviation Maintenance Technician Certification Council) program documents and verifies your military training for the FAA, making it a practical first step in the certification process."}, {"title": "Aviation Maintenance Technician", "description": "You perform scheduled and unscheduled maintenance on aircraft systems, troubleshoot issues, and document all work. This covers avionics, hydraulics, landing gear, and engines depending on your specialty."}, {"title": "Air Traffic Controller", "description": "You direct aircraft in and around airports and airspace using radar and radio communications, keeping separation and sequence. Military ATC experience is directly transferable with FAA licensing. The FAA sets a maximum entry age of 35 for experienced hires; veterans preference can affect this cutoff, so it is worth confirming your situation early in the application process."}, {"title": "Flight Operations Coordinator", "description": "You plan and schedule flight operations, file flight plans, brief crews on weather and route information, and track aircraft movements. This is a ground-based role that uses your aviation knowledge in a planning and coordination capacity."}]
